title: Grade 12 Physics — Electromagnetic Induction
description: Faraday's laws, Lenz's law, motional EMF, inductance, and applications
subject: physics

questions.question: Faraday's First Law of Electromagnetic Induction states that an EMF is induced in a conductor whenever:
options: The magnetic flux through it changes
It is placed near a magnet
questions.explanation: Faraday's First Law: EMF is induced whenever the magnetic flux through a circuit changes. No change in flux = no induced EMF. Key: it's the CHANGE that matters, not the magnitude of flux.

questions.question: Faraday's Second Law: The induced EMF is:
options: Equal to the magnetic field strength
Equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux: ε = −dΦ/dt
Proportional to the area of the coil
questions.explanation: ε = −dΦ/dt (Faraday's 2nd Law). The negative sign is from Lenz's Law. For N turns: ε = −N dΦ/dt.

questions.question: Lenz's Law states that the direction of induced current is such that it:
options: Opposes the change that caused it (Conservation of Energy)
Flows in the direction of external field
questions.explanation: Lenz's Law: induced current creates a magnetic field that OPPOSES the change in flux. This is consistent with conservation of energy (you must do work to change the flux). The negative sign in ε = −dΦ/dt.

questions.question: A conductor of length L moves with velocity v in a magnetic field B (perpendicular). The motional EMF is:
questions.explanation: Motional EMF: ε = BLv. (F = qvB on free charges → charge separation → EMF.) This is the principle of electric generators.

questions.question: Self-inductance (L) is defined such that the induced EMF in a coil is:
questions.explanation: Self-inductance: ε = −L(dI/dt). L is the self-inductance (unit: Henry, H). A coil resists CHANGES in current flowing through itself. Greater L = greater opposition to current change.

questions.question: Energy stored in an inductor with inductance L and current I is:
questions.explanation: Energy in inductor: U = ½LI². Analogous to energy in capacitor: U = ½CV². Both store energy: inductor in magnetic field, capacitor in electric field.

questions.question: Eddy currents are induced in:
options: Conducting materials (solid metal blocks) when flux through them changes — circular induced currents
questions.explanation: Eddy currents: induced in solid conducting masses (metal plates, transformer cores) when magnetic flux changes. They cause heating (loss) and opposing force. Minimised by lamination of iron cores.

questions.question: An AC generator converts:
options: Mechanical energy to electrical energy (using electromagnetic induction)
questions.explanation: AC generator (alternator): mechanical rotation of a coil in a magnetic field induces alternating EMF (Faraday's law). Motor does the reverse: electrical → mechanical.

questions.question: Mutual inductance M between two coils satisfies: ε₂ = ?
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance: ε₂ = −M(dI₁/dt). Changing current in coil 1 induces EMF in coil 2. M depends on geometry, number of turns, and magnetic coupling. Unit: Henry (H). Basis of transformers.

questions.question: A coil of 100 turns has a flux change from 0 to 2 Wb in 4 s. The induced EMF is:
The self-inductance of a solenoid (N turns, length l, cross-section area A) is:
questions.explanation: L = μ₀N²A/l = μ₀n²Al (n = N/l turns per unit length). Increasing N or A or decreasing l increases L. Iron core: multiply by μᵣ.

questions.question: Applications of electromagnetic induction include:
options: Generators, transformers, induction motors, eddy-current brakes, metal detectors, wireless charging
questions.explanation: EMI applications: AC generators (power plants), transformers (voltage conversion), induction motors, electromagnetic brakes, metal detectors, magnetic levitation, induction cookers, wireless charging (Qi).

questions.question: The back-EMF in a motor is due to:
options: The resistance of the motor coil
Electromagnetic induction — the rotating coil itself generates an EMF opposing the applied voltage
questions.explanation: Back-EMF (counter-EMF): as the motor armature spins, it acts as a generator, inducing an EMF opposing the supply (Lenz's Law). Back-EMF limits current: I = (V − ε_back)/R. At startup: back-EMF=0, current is highest.

questions.question: Magnetic flux Φ through a surface is defined as:
options: B · A = BA cos θ (dot product of B and area vector)
questions.explanation: Φ = B · A = BA cos θ where θ is the angle between the magnetic field B and the area normal vector. Maximum flux when B perpendicular to surface (θ=0°); zero when B parallel to surface (θ=90°). Unit: Weber (Wb).

questions.question: Henry (H) as the unit of inductance means:
questions.explanation: 1 Henry = 1 Wb/A = 1 V·s/A = 1 Ω·s. Named after Joseph Henry. From ε = −L(dI/dt): L = |ε/(dI/dt)| = V/(A/s) = V·s/A = Ω·s. Also Φ = LI/N → L = NΦ/I = Wb/A.
